findings.issue_text: [High/concurrency] Narrowing cacheMu to only the final cache assignment permits concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key, duplicating expensive builds and racing to replace the cached index.
[High/concurrency] TotalDocs can read the index cache while BuildIndex concurrently writes it, potentially triggering a concurrent map read/write panic.

goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: [High/concurrency] Narrowing cacheMu to only the final cache assignment permits concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key, duplicating expensive builds and racing to replace the cached index.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies exactly the same problem as the golden comment: the narrowing of cacheMu lock to only protect the final cache assignment (instead of the entire function) allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. Both comments describe the same race condition, the same cause (moving/narrowing the lock), and the same consequence (duplicate expensive builds).

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: [High/concurrency] TotalDocs can read the index cache while BuildIndex concurrently writes it, potentially triggering a concurrent map read/write panic.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same concurrency problem as the golden comment: TotalDocs reading the index cache while BuildIndex concurrently writes to it, which can cause a concurrent map read/write panic. Both comments point to the same race condition between TotalDocs iteration and BuildIndex writes, even though the candidate doesn't explicitly mention the event watcher goroutine as the source of the concurrent BuildIndex calls.
